technique.summary: Inject MongoDB query operators ($gt, $ne, $regex, $where) into application queries to bypass authentication, extract data, or achieve code execution. JSON-based APIs are especially vulnerable when user input is passed directly into query objects.
steps: Identify endpoints that query a NoSQL database (login, search, user lookup)
Test operator injection in JSON body: {"username":{"$ne":""}, "password":{"$ne":""}}
If login bypassed, extract usernames with $regex: {"username":{"$regex":"^a"}}
Use $regex to extract data character by character (blind extraction)
Test for $lookup aggregation injection if using aggregation pipelines

payloads.notes: Authentication bypass — matches any non-empty username and password
Auth bypass for specific user via regex
URL-encoded operator injection for form-based endpoints
$where injection — enables JavaScript execution in query

bypassTechniques: If JSON body is filtered, try query string parameter pollution: user[$ne]=
Use $regex with ReDoS-style patterns for time-based blind extraction
Chain $lookup for cross-collection data access in aggregation pipelines
